findings.claim: The plan-doc §5 example JSON (docs/plans/WP-SCP-023-cross-repo-scorecards.md line ~135) includes a 'signature' field that the implemented schema (schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json) would REJECT. The schema has 'additionalProperties: false' at the root and does not list 'signature' in 'required' or 'properties'. Any emit containing a signature field fails schema validation. The 023C dispatch will read this plan-doc as its specification and may implement an aggregator that expects a signature field.
findings.evidence: plan-doc §5 example JSON (line ~135): '"signature": "<ed25519 signature over the canonicalised payload above, base64>"'. schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json lines 6-19: 'additionalProperties: false' at root; 'required' array lists schema_version/emitted_at/scp_version/repo/ref/commit/verdict/rule_counts/waivers_aggregate/rule_config_aggregate — no 'signature'; 'properties' object has no 'signature' entry. D-041 rationale explicitly states 'no in-payload signature field — platform-level attestation is the trust anchor (per WP-SCP-023 §5 step 3 + D-042 to be filed at slice 023C)'. Release notes v1.2.0.md correctly omit any signature field from the emit shape description. The plan-doc body text at §5 'Signing mechanism' paragraph does acknowledge the OIDC switch, but the JSON shape example at the top of §5 was not updated.
findings.impact: The 023C dispatcher's Opus orchestrator reads the plan-doc §5 as the normative emit contract. If a 023C executor implements the aggregator to expect a 'signature' field and validates each emit against the plan-doc shape, it will reject every 023B emit (which correctly has no signature field). The bug would surface in 023C R1 correctness review but at the cost of a fix round. Per the no-silent-descope invariant: the design shift from in-payload Ed25519 signing to OIDC platform attestation is correct and already captured in D-041/schema/release notes — the plan-doc example is the only stale artifact, but it is the one a 023C implementer reads first.
findings.mitigation: Option A (preferred, inline fix this PR): Remove the '"signature": ...' line from the plan-doc §5 example JSON and add a one-line comment: '// No in-payload signature — OIDC artifact attestation via actions/attest-build-provenance is the trust anchor (see D-042 at 023C)'. Option B (file forward): Add TF-023B-004 to STATUS.md to amend plan-doc §5 example JSON in the next plan-doc maintenance pass. Option A is strongly preferred because the plan-doc is the 023C dispatch reference and will be read before any TF list is consulted.

findings.claim: The DISPATCH-NOTE OUT section (line 34) says 'OIDC attestation generation in the emitter step | Per plan-doc §5 step 3 + D-042 (deferred to slice 023C)' — but the implementation ships an explicit 'Attest scorecard emit (OIDC artifact attestation)' step using actions/attest-build-provenance@a2bbfa25... # v4.1.0. The DISPATCH-NOTE's OUT entry conflates two distinct things: (1) the in-payload Ed25519 signature (correctly OUT), and (2) the platform-level OIDC artifact attestation action (actually IN this slice as step 4 of 4). STATUS.md correctly documents '4 new gated steps: Build scorecard emit + Validate against schema + Upload artifact + actions/attest-build-provenance@v4.1.0 OIDC attestation'. The DISPATCH-NOTE is the primary scope-boundary document and readers will see a contradiction.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md lines 34-35: OUT item 'OIDC attestation generation in the emitter step | Per plan-doc §5 step 3 + D-042 (deferred to slice 023C — the aggregator is the verification side). 023B emits the artifact; 023C verifies via gh attestation verify --signer-workflow. The artifact is already covered by Actions Artifact Attestation when emitted by SHA-pinned reusable workflows (the platform-level attestation; not an in-emit signature).' policy-check.yml lines 1468-1472: 'name: Attest scorecard emit (OIDC artifact attestation)' uses: 'actions/attest-build-provenance@a2bbfa25375fe432b6a289bc6b6cd05ecd0c4c32 # v4.1.0'. STATUS.md 023B row: 'actions/attest-build-provenance@v4.1.0 OIDC attestation' listed as step 4 of 4.
findings.impact: Future reviewers reading the DISPATCH-NOTE will flag 'OIDC attestation is OUT' as a scope boundary violation since the workflow includes an explicit attest step. This creates confusion at 023C dispatch time when the orchestrator reconciles the DISPATCH-NOTE against the actual workflow. Practically harmless — the implementation is correct — but the documentation misaligns with the governance convention that the DISPATCH-NOTE is the authoritative scope record.
findings.mitigation: Amend DISPATCH-NOTE OUT entry to distinguish the two concepts: 'In-payload Ed25519 signature | Superseded by OIDC artifact attestation (actions/attest-build-provenance@v4.1.0) which IS in scope as step 4 of 4 in this slice — the attestation EMISSION side lands in 023B; the aggregator VERIFICATION side (gh attestation verify --signer-workflow) lands in 023C per D-042 reservation.' Alternatively, move the attest step to the IN scope table with a brief rationale. Either fix removes the contradiction.

findings.claim: The 'How to verify' section in docs/releases/v1.2.0.md shows 'gh attestation verify scorecard-emit.json' but 'gh run download <run-id> --name scorecard-emit' (without --dir flag) extracts the artifact into a subdirectory named after the artifact ('scorecard-emit/scorecard-emit.json'), not to 'scorecard-emit.json' in the current directory. The preceding 'cat scorecard-emit.json | jq ...' command would also fail. This was the category of error caught at 023A R3 (wrong flag name); this instance is wrong path rather than wrong flag.
findings.evidence: docs/releases/v1.2.0.md lines 74-79: 'gh run download <run-id> --name scorecard-emit' then 'cat scorecard-emit.json | jq ...' then 'gh attestation verify scorecard-emit.json --signer-workflow ...'. GitHub CLI gh run download behavior: without --dir, artifact named 'scorecard-emit' containing file 'scorecard-emit.json' is extracted to './scorecard-emit/scorecard-emit.json'. The artifact was uploaded at policy-check.yml line 1464-1465 with name: 'scorecard-emit', path: 'output/scorecards/scorecard-emit.json' — the path within the artifact is 'scorecard-emit.json' (no directory prefix), so the downloaded layout is 'scorecard-emit/scorecard-emit.json'.
findings.impact: An adopter or auditor following the 'How to verify' instructions will get 'No such file or directory' on both the cat and gh attestation verify commands. Since the primary purpose of this section is to give verifiable proof of OIDC attestation, a broken example undermines the supply-chain verification story at exactly the moment an auditor would try to use it.
findings.mitigation: Correct the verify section to: 'gh run download <run-id> --name scorecard-emit' then 'cat scorecard-emit/scorecard-emit.json | jq ...' then 'gh attestation verify scorecard-emit/scorecard-emit.json --signer-workflow jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<sha>'. Alternatively add '--dir .' flag and note that with --dir . the file lands at './scorecard-emit.json' directly. Confirm the correct path empirically in the 023C canary run and update release notes before tag cut.

findings.claim: The workflow-selftest harness (tests/workflow/fixture-{pass,fail}/) does not include a fixture-pass-with-scorecard-emit case for the new opt-in input. The gap is acknowledged in the test docstring of tests/scorecard-emit/test_scorecard_emit_schema.py ('The end-to-end transformation (policy-check-summary → scorecard-emit) is integration-tested by the workflow-selftest harness when the SCP self-dogfood wrapper opts in to scorecard-emit: true (forward-compat to slice 023C)') but no TF is filed in STATUS.md.
findings.evidence: tests/scorecard-emit/test_scorecard_emit_schema.py lines 20-23 (docstring): 'The end-to-end transformation (policy-check-summary → scorecard-emit) is integration-tested by the workflow-selftest harness when the SCP self-dogfood wrapper opts in to scorecard-emit: true (forward-compat to slice 023C).' Glob of tests/workflow/: fixture-pass/ and fixture-fail/ exist with services.yml and expected-annotations.json pairs — no scorecard-emit fixture. STATUS.md: no TF-023B-001 or equivalent entry for workflow-selftest extension. DISPATCH-NOTE: does not address the workflow-selftest gap.
findings.impact: The workflow-selftest harness is the integration-level gate that exercises the full policy-check.yml flow end-to-end. Without a scorecard-emit fixture, the 4 new gated steps (build + validate + upload + attest) are only tested by the unit-level pytest schema-validation tests, not by an actual Actions workflow run. A regression in the workflow's Python heredoc (e.g. env var path substitution failure, yaml.safe_load import path change) would not be caught by the existing harness. This is the acknowledged gap that the docstring defers.
findings.mitigation: File TF-023B-001 in STATUS.md: 'Workflow-selftest harness fixture-pass-with-scorecard-emit — add a fixture that exercises scorecard-emit: true in the SCP self-dogfood wrapper (policy-check-wrapper.yml). Closes the integration-test gap acknowledged in test_scorecard_emit_schema.py docstring.' Do NOT descope the unit-level pytest tests in place of this — they remain the primary schema-conformance gate; the selftest is the integration gate.

findings.claim: The 'Upload scorecard emit artifact' (step 3) and 'Attest scorecard emit' (step 4) steps are gated on 'steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == success' but NOT on 'steps.validate-scorecard-emit.outcome == success'. A schema-invalid emit (e.g. produced by a commit field that is an empty string, failing the 40-char hex pattern) would still be uploaded and attested before the validate step's failure marks the job red.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 1461: 'if: inputs.scorecard-emit && steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == success'. Line 1469: same gate. Line 1438: validate step gate is 'if: inputs.scorecard-emit && steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == success' (correct dependency direction but upload/attest don't chain onto validate). The Python build step at line 1297 reads 'commit = summary.get("pr_sha", "")' — if pr_sha is absent or empty the emit will be written with an invalid commit field; the build step exits zero (file was written); validate step fails; upload and attest run on the invalid file because they only check build.outcome.
findings.impact: In practice the job would be red (validate failed), so 023C's aggregator (which only reads successful runs) would skip the emit. The invalid emit artifact would exist in the store but would not be consumed. Defense-in-depth gap only — no governance-bypass scenario. The DISPATCH-NOTE doesn't specify the exact gate chain, so this is an implementation choice rather than an AC violation.
findings.mitigation: Change upload and attest step conditions from 'steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == success' to 'steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == success && steps.validate-scorecard-emit-against-schema.outcome == success' (using the step id of the validate step). This is a two-line change. Alternatively, file TF-023B-002 to address in 023C when the workflow is next touched.

AC (viii) 'pytest passes' and AC (ix) 'pre-push wrapper passes' are verified by structural inspection (test file exists, fixture dirs exist, test imports and parametrization match FIXTURES_ROOT, pre-push wrapper script exists from TF-020P-005 at PR #94) but not by runtime execution. I could not independently verify the gh run download artifact extraction path (CG-MIN-002). Different gh CLI versions may extract to different paths. The finding is based on standard GitHub CLI artifact download semantics, but should be confirmed empirically before the tag cut.

The DISPATCH-NOTE's OIDC attestation OUT entry (CG-MIN-001) is ambiguous — it could be read as 'in-payload signature OUT' (correct) or 'all OIDC attestation OUT' (incorrect given the explicit actions/attest-build-provenance step). I interpreted it as the former based on the surrounding context ('not an in-emit signature'), but the wording is genuinely unclear and could mislead a future reviewer.

The verdict derivation in the Python heredoc (policy-check.yml lines 1337-1343) treats any rule with raw_findings > 0 and denies == 0 and waived == 0 and not rule_config_disabled as a 'warn' verdict. Whether warn-baseline rule findings appear with verdict=='deny' or verdict!='deny' in the policy-check-summary.json depends on the SCP-R-004 implementation in policies/SCP-R-004.rego. I did not read the Rego rule to confirm. This is a correctness-lens concern that may be addressed in the parallel R1 correctness review.

The workflow-level 'attestations: write' and 'id-token: write' permissions (policy-check.yml lines 71-72) apply to ALL workflow steps, not just the scorecard-emit gated steps. Non-opt-in adopters will have these permissions declared for their workflow runs (though the attest action is gated and never invoked). The release notes say these permissions are 'unused by adopters who do NOT opt in' — this is accurate for the action invocation but the OIDC token endpoint is still accessible to all 'run:' bash steps in the job. This is a safety-lens concern primarily; from a completeness perspective the release notes are accurate but could be more precise.
summary: 14 of 17 ACs satisfied at code level; 3 process-pending (xv–xvii). The schema, workflow, tests, version bump, release notes, D-041 row, STATUS.md row, VERSIONING.md extension, and CODEOWNERS coverage are all correct and complete. D-041 accurately captures all five required elements (data shape, opt-in posture, MAJOR-pinning, gh attestation verify --signer-workflow, v1.2.0 cut). Tag-cut process is sound (release-gate.yml pre-exists; v1.2.0 cut is post-merge; AC xvii is correctly process-pending). Forward-compat with 023C is confirmed (artifact name 'scorecard-emit', path 'output/scorecards/scorecard-emit.json'). Cross-repo notification is correctly deferred — no adopter has opted in, so ACC/CT/mapp-estate-regression have nothing to act on; notification belongs at 023D-onboarding. ADOPT-001 §13 OUT is sound. Schema versioning (v0.1 const, MAJOR-pinned, aggregator drops unknown schema_version) is documented in schema, D-041, and release notes. R-023-07 and R-023-08 risk rows are addressed. One MAJ blocks approval: the plan-doc §5 example JSON retains a stale 'signature' field that the implemented schema (additionalProperties: false, no 'signature' in required or properties) would reject — misleading for the 023C dispatch. Five MIN findings cover: DISPATCH-NOTE OUT section conflates in-payload signing with the OIDC attestation step that IS shipped; 'How to verify' attestation verify path likely wrong; D-040/D-041 rows swapped in DECISIONS.md table; TF-023A-002 (cross-repo notification) not referenced or explicitly deferred; and workflow-selftest harness gap not filed as TF.
